rules.message: nldd-avatar-group sizes, stacks and rings its avatars, so it only takes nldd-avatar.
Every child of nldd-bar-split-view needs a `slot`, or it does not render.
nldd-button-group holds three buttons at most; the rest are hidden.
nldd-button needs `text` or `accessible-label`, otherwise it has no accessible name.
A card that is a link or button needs `accessible-label`: the control has no text of its own.
Put the action in a nldd-button-group, also when there is only one.
nldd-form-field holds no form input, so the label has nothing to connect to.
nldd-icon-button needs `text` or `accessible-label`, otherwise it has no accessible name.
A row takes cells and segments. Anything else sits outside its layout.
nldd-list-item needs a parent nldd-list, which gives the row its type and keyboard behaviour.
A modal dialog with one action leaves nothing to choose: it needs a way out as well.
nldd-page-footer has its own slot on nldd-page and sets its own width and spacing.
Render nldd-sheet at the document root: inside a pane it is clipped by that pane.
A website lets its header scroll away: a fixed one takes room from the content.
A button bar holds actions, not toggles: an active toggle looks like a pressed action here.
nldd-popover needs `accessible-label`, or a screen reader announces it without a name.
nldd-tab-bar needs `accessible-label`, so a screen reader can say what the tabs are for.
nldd-table needs `columns`, a CSS grid track list, or its cells do not line up.
nldd-table needs `accessible-label`: role="table" takes its name from there.
Tabs with `href` go to another page: add `navigation`, so the bar is a nav and not a tablist.
Give this item an alternative in `slot="overflow"`: on a narrow screen it moves to the overflow menu, and without one it is gone.
